newsitem.title: USA: Psychiatric says Q1 funds could drop.
newsitem.headline: Psychiatric says Q1 funds could drop.

text.p: Psychiatric Group of American Health Properties Inc said on Thursday first quarter funds from operations could drop $0.05 per share because of difficulties at The Manors facility in Tarpon Springs, Fla.
The company said the operational difficulties meant the operator of the facility had not made its February payment.

Assuming no further rent or interest payments from The Manors for the first quarter of 1997, FFO for that quarter would decrease by $0.05 per share compared to the fourth quarter of 1996, it said. Total FFO for the fourth quarter for the Psychiatric Group was $0.87 per share, it said.
Psychiatric said it has been told that the census for January at the facility was significantly below the levels projected by the operator at year-end.

Although the operator did make its rental payment of $50,000 in January ($0.02 of FFO per Psychiatric Group depositary share) and had made its rent payments during the fourth quarter of 1996, the operator has not made its February payment, it said.
During 1996, The Manors' paid total restructured rent and interest payments of $217,000, representing FFO of $0.10 per share or 3.3 percent of the Psychiatric Group's total FFO.
This impact on FFO solely relates to the FFO of the Psychiatric Group and has no bearing on the Core Group's FFO, it said.

During the past two weeks, a new executive director and marketing director for The Manors have been put in place by the owner and operator, and the name of the facility has recently been changed to Northpointe Behavioral Health Systems.

Psychiatric said there can be no assurances that the efforts under way will be successful in rebuilding the census and cash flow for 1997 to a level sufficient to allow the facility to meet its obligations.
The company said it remains committed to maximising the value of its investment in The Manors and believes the highest value for the facility would likely be as a health care facility.
However, it said it also evaluating a range of possibilities, including alternative uses for the facility and its related land.
